packageRules.description: fastmcp is deliberately locked to a 4.0 pre-release while 4.0 is in beta (see the [tool.uv] prerelease note in the root pyproject). Every bump — beta to beta, or beta to GA — swaps the MCP protocol layer under both servers, so it always gets human review instead of automerging.

customManagers.description: The omnigraph binary version, pinned in THREE places that must move together: witan-core's shared installer (what `witan setup` fetches onto a developer's PATH), and the two Dockerfiles (what the deployed data tier and the MCP tier's bundled CLI run). A partial bump ships a client and a server on different releases, and omnigraph uses strict single-version storage — a 0.8.x binary refuses a 0.9.x graph and vice versa — so a split-version deploy is a hard outage, not a soft degradation. `just check-omnigraph-pins` enforces agreement in CI as a backstop. NOTE THE BLIND SPOT while the repo tracks the moving `edge` tag: the version pin declares what the `edge` build REPORTS, so upstream cutting that version for real compares equal to `currentValue` and raises nothing here. `.github/workflows/omnigraph-release-watch.yml` covers that case.
